subject: DRINK
text: The DRINK command allows a warrior to use a HEAL or PURE potion on another warrior in battle.

evidence.quote: DRINK: use a HEAL or PURE potion on another warrior

subject: ITEM
text: Using an item from inventory in battle does not destroy it, and warriors do not need to be able to equip it to use it.

evidence.quote:
ITEM: use an item in that warrior's weapons or armor inventory as an item in
	battle.  Using items in this way doesn't destroy the item.  It is not
	necessary to equip the item or even to be able to equip it in order
	for a warrior to be able to use it as an item

subject: RUN
text: If any warrior successfully uses the RUN command in battle, the entire party escapes.

evidence.quote:
RUN: run away from battle.  If any warrior in your party does this
	successfully, your entire party escapes

subject: Battle Actions
text: Actions targeted at dead or stoned characters are ineffective but still consume resources like spell charges or potions.

evidence.quote:
all actions which end up being targeted to dead or stoned characters are
ineffective.  Any action which is ineffective still uses the resources put
into the action, such as a spell charge or potion.

subject: Battle Actions
text: An action interrupted by incapacitation or early battle termination is considered to have never happened, so resources are not wasted.

evidence.quote:
An action which is
interrupted due to incapacitation of the actor or early termination of battle
is considered to have never happened, and thus the resources put into it are
not wasted

subject: Monster Magic
text: When a monster casts magic, it follows a unique circular spell cycle that always begins in the same place.

evidence.quote:
if it chooses to use magic(if it has that capability), it casts the next spell
available in its cycle.  Each monster has a unique circular list of magic
spells that always begins in the same place.

subject: Monster Special Attacks
text: Monsters execute special attacks using a circular cycle that runs independently alongside their magic cycle.

evidence.quote:
if it chooses to launch a special attack(if it has this capability), it does
the next one available in its cycle of special attacks.  This cycle works just
like the magic cycle.  Both cycles may run simultaneously but they don't
affect each another.

subject: Monster Targeting
text: Single-target attacks pick the front warrior on a 1..4 roll, second warrior on 5..6, third on 7, and fourth on 8.

evidence.quote:
if the action was an attack, or a magical or a special attack that was
directed towards a single warrior, the monster generates a random number,
x = (1..8).  If x:(1..4) the target of the attack is the warrior in front.  If
x:(5..6), the target is the second warrior.  x = 7 is the third warrior and
x = 8 is the fourth warrior.

subject: Hit Count
text: Maximum hits per attack is [H%/32]+1 for most classes, or 2 x ([H%/32]+1) for an unarmed Black Belt or Master.

evidence.quote:
N(h) = [H%/32]+1 for all classes, except...
     = 2 x ([H%/32]+1) for an unarmed Bb/Ma

subject: Attack Damage
text: Each hit that connects deals (D..Dx2) - A damage, with critical hits adding Dx2 to the damage.

evidence.quote:
for each hit that gets through, damage done = (D..Dx2) - A, using the
attacker's D and the defender's A....Now, if by chance
the hit was a critical hit, add Dx2 to the damage done.

subject: Magic Damage
text: Damaging magic attacks have base power M dealing [M/4]..M damage, which reduces to [M/8]..[M/4] against resistance and increases to [3M/8]..[3M/2] against weakness.

evidence.quote:
every magical or special attack that does damage has a base power, call it M.
From this, the actual damage done = ([M/4]..M).  This damage cannot be
absorbed with armor.  If the target is resistant to the attack, damage done =
([M/8]..[M/4])*.  If the target is weak against the attack, damage done =
([3M/8]..[3M/2]).  Magical and special attacks which inflict damage never miss

subject: Elemental Resistance
text: Due to a bug, granting elemental resistance to a target that is naturally weak to that element has no effect and damage is still calculated using weakness.

evidence.quote:
BUG: if a target is weak vs. a certain elemental, giving that target
	resistance has no effect - damage done is still applied as if the
	target was weak vs. that elemental.

subject: Experience
text: Battle XP is divided equally among alive and non-stoned warriors up to a maximum of 999999 XP.

evidence.quote:
XP gained from battle is the direct sum of all XP values of monsters killed.
If there are N warriors which are not stoned or dead, each one of them gets
[(total XP)/N] experience points....If XP
for any warrior exceeds 999999 at any time, XP = 999999

subject: Gold
text: Battle GOLD is added directly to the party's supply, which is capped at 999999.

evidence.quote:
GOLD gained from battle is the direct sum of the GOLD values of all monsters
killed.  This is added to the party's GOLD supply.  If the GOLD supply exceeds
999999 at any time, GOLD = 999999

subject: Vehicle Speed
text: On the world map, walking and canoe speed is 2.1 steps/second, ship speed is 7.5 steps/second, and airspeed is 15 steps/second.

evidence.quote:
walking ( = canoe speed)	= 2.1 steps/second
shipspeed 			= 7.5 steps/second
airspeed			= 15 steps/second

subject: Posture
text: A warrior adopts a kneeling posture in battle when HP drops below [MHP/4].

evidence.quote: if a warrior's HP<[MHP/4], that warrior will adopt a kneeling posture

subject: Status Ailments
text: Finishing battle with a permanent ailment like POISON, STONE, or death automatically switches that warrior to the back of the party.

evidence.quote:
Any warrior which finishes a
battle with a permanent condition such as POISON, STONE, or death is
automatically switched with the warrior in the back of the party

subject: MUTE
text: Muted warriors cannot use ITEM, MAGIC, or DRINK actions, and muted enemies cannot use magical or special attacks.

evidence.quote:
MUTE(nP): all ITEM, MAGIC, and DRINK actions of a muted warrior will be
	ineffective (including the AMUT spell).  All magical or special
	attacks of a muted enemy will be ineffective

subject: POISON
text: Poison causes a warrior to lose 1 HP per step outside combat and 2 HP per round in battle.

evidence.quote:
POISON(Pm): outside of battle, a poisoned warrior will lose 1 HP with every
	step, whether the step is taken inside or outside (HP may not sink
	below 1 from this)...In battle, the
	warrior loses 2 HP every round and may die because of this.

subject: STONE
text: Stoned warriors cannot act or be targeted, enemies hit with stone die instantly, and stoning a warrior removes poison.

evidence.quote:
STONE(Pm): a stoned warrior may take no actions and may not be the target of
	enemy actions.  A stoned enemy dies instantly.  If all warriors become
	STONE or dead, your party perishes.  Stoning a warrior removes POISON

subject: Slain
text: A dead warrior lies face down, cannot act or be targeted, has HP set to 0, and has poison removed.

evidence.quote:
(slain)(Pm): a dead warrior may take no actions and may not be the target of
	enemy actions. Killing a warrior removes POISON.  To be dead is to lie
	face to the ground.  Death automatically sets HP = 0

subject: Magic Spells
text: Eligibility to buy a magic spell is determined by character class, with combat-only spells marked Cb and non-combat spells marked nC.

evidence.quote:
the capability to buy a particular magic spell for use in casting is
determined by character class.  The classes which are eligible to learn the 
spell are listed in the 'Who' column.  Some spells have different effects
based on whether combat is ensuing or not.  'Cb' in the 'Use' column means
that the described effect only happens if the spell is cast in combat.  'nC'
means that the effect only happens outside of combat.

what levels your warriors are at.  Resurrection is the same as casting the
LIFE spell on the dead warrior, and the cost of this also remains constant
throughout the game at any given location
